title: Open Virtualization Console
description: Opens the host's Virtualization console window so the user can view virtual machine state. Gated by the virtualization.view capability grant.

title: Open Terminal
description: Opens SwiftCode's real Terminal view — a full interactive shell (local shells, SSH nodes, themes), not a sandbox. HIGH-RISK: requires explicit user approval of the sandbox.view grant.

title: Open Deployments Console
description: Opens SwiftCode's real Deployments console (Netlify, Vercel, GitHub Pages). HIGH-RISK: deployments change production; requires explicit user approval of the deployConsole.view grant.

title: Open Database Explorer
description: Opens the real Database Explorer window for browsing the open project's databases. Querying happens through the explorer's own UI and host-mediated connections.

title: Use SwiftCode Cloud Model
description: Runs one completion through the host-mediated SwiftCode Cloud Model and logs the answer. Requires the use.SwiftCodeModel grant; the call counts against the user's daily quota and the extension never sees credentials.

title: Run Sandboxed Command
description: Runs one allow-listed command through the host's sandboxed execution service — no shell, no terminal UI, working directory confined to the project scope, hard timeout, byte-capped output. Requires the terminal.sandbox grant.

title: Open CI Workflows
description: Opens the CI / visual workflow dashboard to inspect pipelines and workflow graphs for the open project. Read-only window into the surface — it does not trigger pipeline runs.

title: Inspect Repository Status and Diff
description: Reads the working-tree status snapshot (branch, ahead/behind, staged and unstaged counts) and a bounded unified diff of the changes, then logs a summary. Strictly read-only via source-control.read.

title: Run Project Build
description: Starts a build of the given target through the host's managed build service, streams the live output events to the log, and reports the real terminal result (status, exit code, diagnostics). Requires the build.execute grant.

title: Open Simulator Workspace
description: Opens the Simulator workspace to view and interact with booted simulators. Simulator management stays inside the workspace's own UI.

title: Open Live SwiftUI Preview
description: Opens the live SwiftUI preview surface, which compiles project views through the host's managed preview pipeline.

title: Open Visual UI Builder
description: Opens the Visual UI Builder for composing interfaces. Applying changes to the project happens through the builder's own flow, not through the extension.

title: Browse SF Symbols
description: Opens the SF Symbol picker so the user can browse and pick system symbols. Purely informational, low-risk surface.

title: Search Documentation
description: Opens the documentation browser to search and read developer documentation. Read-only reference access.

title: Open Coding Dictionary
description: Opens the coding dictionary for quick reference on APIs and language terms. Read-only reference access.

title: Open Device Connect
description: Opens the Device Connect surface for managing paired Apple devices. Device operations stay inside Device Connect's own controls.

title: Register Extension Command
description: Registers a command that appears in the host's interface — the supported UI contribution for extensions. The host also removes all registrations on deactivation.

title: Read Current Project
description: Reads safe metadata about the currently open project (name, id, root path). Never carries file contents.

title: Store a Secret (Security)
description: Stores a secret in the macOS Keychain under the app's Security ID by triggering the host's secure popup — the user types the secret directly into the host, so extension code never sees it. Resolves with metadata only ({valueID, created}). Requires the use.Security grant.

title: Use a Stored Secret for an API Call
description: Asks the host to perform an HTTPS request with a stored secret attached as the Authorization header. The host performs the request and returns only {status, body} — the secret never comes back to extension code. Requires the use.Security grant.
